title: Stacked header collapse and inline density toggle for responsive virtual table
creator: Marina Voss
description: Context: As we expand the virtualized table component to support denser dashboards and narrower layouts, product teams keep requesting: (1) a robust way to display multi-level column headers without consuming vertical real estate, and (2) an easy inline control for users to switch density without visiting a separate settings panel. This ticket proposes: a stacked header pattern that can collapse into a single-line header per column on demand, paired with an inline density toggle (Compact / Comfortable / Readable) that persists per-user and integrates with our design tokens. Goals: reduce header height for dense views, maintain discoverability of grouped columns, keep keyboard and screen-reader accessibility, and avoid regressions in virtualization performance.
acceptance_criteria: Stacked header groups render in virtualized table rows and collapse to single-line labels when collapsed state is active
Inline density toggle appears in the table toolbar and changes spacing, font-size tokens, and row height in real time
Collapsed header state and selected density persist across page reloads per user via local preference storage and platform setting (fall back to tenant default)
Keyboard interactions: toggle header collapse via keyboard shortcut (Shift+H) and cycle density with (D), all announced through an aria-live region
Performance: no measurable increase in average row render time > 10% for 10k-row tables when collapse is toggled
Accessibility: screen readers correctly read grouped headers when expanded and announce collapse/expand state changes
Visual QA: tokens updated and documented for three density modes (compact+, compact, readable) and approved by design token owner
Design handoff: Figma frames, CSS token mappings, and a usage doc in Confluence are linked in this ticket
design_notes: Pattern summary: each header group can be in one of three states: expanded (stacked lines showing group label + sub-labels), compact-expanded (single line with a chevron to reveal sub-labels on hover/focus), collapsed (single primary label). The inline density toggle adjusts: --token-row-padding-vertical, --token-row-gap, --token-font-size-base, and --token-icon-size. We will add a small, persistent affordance in the top-right of the table toolbar: an icon with a segmented control that reveals density names on hover. For very narrow viewports, collapsed headers should auto-apply and present a tooltip on first use explaining density toggle. Use the new spacing tokens introduced in tokens-2026 and map legacy table classes to the new vars. Edge cases: pinned columns must mirror collapse state; frozen header shadows should not reflow layout when collapsing/expanding; column resize handles must remain reachable when headers are one-line.
decisions: Use client-side localStorage key 'rw.table.v2.userPrefs' to persist density and headerCollapse for hosted product; Dedicated/Private customers can override via tenant config
Expose two new tokens: --rw-table-density and --rw-table-header-line-height instead of per-mode CSS classes to simplify runtime switching
Keyboard shortcut choices: Shift+H for header collapse to reduce conflicts, 'D' to cycle density (documented in keyboard help)
tasks: Design: create Figma frames for three density modes and three header states + narrow breakpoint variants
Design: write accessibility spec for screen readers and aria-live messaging
Engineering: prototype collapse animation in storybook using virtualized row samples
Engineering: integrate token vars and ensure batch render performance is not regressed
QA: run render-time perf bench with 1k/10k/50k rows and capture median render time before/after
Docs: author 'Table: Density and Stacked Headers' usage doc in Confluence and add to component catalog
